page: dashboard, recipes, recipes/new, focus, collection, projects/[id]
principle: Refactoring UI — Hierarchy / Von Restorff Effect; project convention MM-52 ("+ rule")
relatesTo: Comment-audit item #1 (all + buttons neon green except wishlist yellow)
problem: The neon-green 'add' button variant exists (Button.tsx variant='add', glow-green) but is used ONLY in /gallery. Every real add/+ button in the app renders CYAN instead of green. Confirmed live: '+ New Project' uses the default 'primary' (cyan) variant; '+ RECIPE', '+ ADD SLOT', '+ ADD PAINT', '+ DATE', '+ PAINT' are built from raw cyan classes. Only the per-row project '+' add-slot on the dashboard table is green (computed rgb(81,253,128)).
fix: Adopt variant="add" on every add/+ button: '+ New Project' (DashboardView.tsx:107 -> <Button variant="add">), '+ RECIPE' (RecipeIndexTable + header), '+ ADD SLOT' (RecipeEditorView), '+ ADD PAINT' (CollectionView), '+ DATE' (PlannerCalendar/RightRail), '+ PAINT'/'+ Add paint' (Focus PaintCard), '+ SUB-PROJECT'. Use variant="addWishlist" (yellow) only on wishlist add buttons. Leave the '◎ Focus' action cyan (it is not an add).

principle: NN/g #7 Flexibility & efficiency; Peak-End Rule; Figma Recipe.png
relatesTo: Comment-audit item #2 (recipe paint click should open full recipe-creator toolset)
screenshot: recipe-detail-live-desktop.png, library-paint-info-desktop.png (the rich toolset that ISN'T wired into recipes)
problem: Clicking a recipe paint slot does NOT open the full recipe-creator toolset (colour wheel + match + filterable library + dropper + layering). The recipe editor only shows a slot row with a stage <select> ('Basecoat') and a note input. The rich PAINT INFO panel (HEX, harmonies, MATCH across brands, similar-in-other-brands) that the Figma Recipe.png ref specifies — and which already exists for the Library (PaintInfoPanelContent.tsx) — is not reachable from the recipe builder. The recipe paint picker is a reduced selector, not the full toolset.
fix: Wire the existing PaintInfoPanelContent / SlideOutPanel (and the tools: ColourWheelTool, ColourMatchTool, EyedropperTool, LayeringTool, filterable SwatchWall) into the recipe slot interaction so clicking a slot opens the full creator. Reuse the Library paint-info drawer rather than rebuilding. Match the Figma Recipe.png right-rail panel layout.

principle: NN/g #1 Visibility of system status; matches FocusView projectMinutes contract (A5qzb)
problem: FocusView accepts a projectMinutes prop and renders 'Time {formatMinutes(projectMinutes)}' in the pinned-project header when non-null (line 103). But focus/page.tsx never passes projectMinutes, so per-project time never appears. Live render of the pinned header shows 'SALAMANDERS 2K x0' with no Time. The only time shown (SESSION panel: Today/Week/Streak) is global, not per-project.
fix: In focus/page.tsx, sum the logged session minutes for the focused project (and its sub-projects) and pass it as projectMinutes to <FocusView />. The render path already exists — this is a data-wiring fix only.

principle: NN/g #2 Match between system & real world; Refactoring UI — labels/values; Figma collection.png
problem: The paint collection table columns are [Image, Name, Company, Vendor, Price, Recipe, Status, Link]. There is no paint 'Type' column (Contrast / Wash / Acrylic / Layer / ...). A 'Recipe' (attach) column occupies that slot instead. Painters reason about paints by type, and the Library paint-info panel already exposes TYPE (e.g. 'Acrylic'), so the data exists.
fix: Add a 'Type' column to PAINT_COLS and render the paint's type (same value shown as TYPE in PaintInfoPanelContent). Decide whether 'Recipe' attach stays a column or moves into the row's action cluster.

principle: Consistency & standards; CRT §9 palette roles; project MM-19
relatesTo: Comment-audit item #3 (wishlist button yellow, not cyan)
problem: In the Library LIST table, the wishlist toggle text color is yellow when active but the class string is 'text-yellow text-glow-cyan' — it still carries the cyan glow from before the yellow conversion. Base color is correct (yellow); the leftover cyan glow is the reported inconsistency. The Library paint-info panel wishlist button (PaintInfoPanelContent.tsx:119-124) IS correctly all-yellow, so only the list-table cell is wrong.
fix: PaintListTable.tsx:95 — change 'text-yellow text-glow-cyan' to 'text-yellow text-glow-yellow' (or drop the glow). Align with the all-yellow treatment in PaintInfoPanelContent.

principle: CRT §9 phosphor treatment; Refactoring UI — hierarchy via depth
relatesTo: Comment-audit item #7 (stat numbers shadow/outline retro treatment)
location: src/components/kit/StatBox.tsx (value div uses accentText only, no glow/shadow)
problem: Dashboard stat numbers render in flat accent colour (confirmed live multi-colour: Active green, Completion yellow, Streak purple, Time cyan — the multi-colour intent IS met) but have NO phosphor glow / text-shadow / outline. The terminal aesthetic (DESIGN_LANGUAGE.md, BEST-PRACTICES §9) calls for a phosphor text-shadow on hero numerics; these big readouts are the natural place for it and currently read flat against the black canvas.
fix: Add a per-accent phosphor text-shadow to the StatBox value (e.g. text-glow-{accent}) so each big number gets a soft glow matching its hue. Keep base colour unchanged (contrast is measured on base colour, already passes). Static glow only — no flicker.

principle: NN/g #4 Consistency & standards; themed-control fidelity; Figma collection.png (styled status pills)
relatesTo: Comment-audit item #8 (project-assignment dropdown styled vs native <select>)
problem: Project-assignment and status dropdowns are plain native <select> elements (browser-rendered chevron + native OS option list), only lightly styled with an accent border/text. In the terminal aesthetic the native popup is a stark OS-chrome rectangle that breaks the illusion. The Figma collection.png shows styled status pills (coloured WISHLIST/OWNED chips), not native selects. Confirmed on Focus '+ Focus', Recipe 'PROJECT' column, Recipe-editor 'ASSIGN TO PROJECT', Collection status, and project-detail TYPE/STATUS/PRIORITY.
fix: Replace native <select> with one shared themed dropdown primitive (custom button + role=listbox/option, full keyboard support) rendering options in phosphor style. Reuse across all five surfaces. Preserve keyboard operability and aria-label.

page: dashboard (39 targets), tools-stacking (15), recipes table, planner, collection
location: ProjectsTable expand '>' (20x20) + 'Change attached recipe' (16x16) + '+ attach' (h20); MiniCalendar arrows (24x20); tools-stacking controls
problem: 39 interactive targets on the dashboard are under the WCAG 2.2 minimum of 24x24 CSS px (row-expand toggle 20x20, 'Change attached recipe' 16x16, calendar nav arrows 24x20 height, '+ attach' 72x20 height). tools-stacking has 15 sub-24px targets. These cause measurable tap errors on touch, which matters because the app reflows to a mobile layout.
fix: Bump these controls to >=24x24 (ideally 44x44 on touch) via padding or min-h/min-w. For icon toggles use a 24px+ hit area around a smaller glyph. Prioritise the dashboard row controls and calendar arrows.

problem: The active PAINT/MODEL kind toggle renders black text (rgb(0,0,0)) on a dark accent fill, measured at 1.05:1 — far below the 4.5:1 AA minimum for the 10px label. The active segment label is effectively unreadable.
fix: Fill the active segment with a bright accent so black text hits >=4.5:1, OR switch the active label to a light colour on the dark fill. Verify with a contrast tool after the change.

problem: Sign-in and sign-up have no semantic heading (h1-h6 count = 0). 'SYS > ACCESS' is a decorative panel label and 'MINI-MANAGER OS v1.0' is body text. Screen-reader users get no page heading to orient on. (Inputs ARE properly labelled — USERNAME/PASSWORD labels above fields, not placeholder-only.)
fix:
Add a visually-styled or visually-hidden

to each auth page (e.g.

Sign in to Mini Manager

), or promote 'SYS > ACCESS' to an h1 keeping its terminal styling.

principle: NN/g #1 Visibility of system status; missing-feature
relatesTo: Comment-audit item #5 (dashboard per-project time totals from logged focus sessions)
problem: No per-project time total is surfaced on the dashboard. StatRow shows a single global 'Time Total'; the projects table has no logged-time column, and the project-detail page has no time readout. Painters can't see time spent per project from logged focus sessions. (Dashboard companion to UX-003.)
fix: Surface logged minutes per project: a compact time column/badge on ProjectsTable rows and/or a 'Time' readout on project-detail, from the same per-project session aggregation needed for UX-003. Reuse formatMinutes().

principle: Consistency & standards; themed-control fidelity (same class as UX-007)
problem: The project-detail TARGET DATE field is a native date input rendering US 'mm/dd/yyyy' format regardless of locale — inconsistent with the rest of the themed UI and a minor i18n issue for a UK-based product. Native date-picker chrome also breaks the terminal aesthetic.
fix: Replace native <input type=date> with a themed date control, or at minimum format display to the product's locale. Pair with the themed-control work in UX-007.

principle: Doherty Threshold; Refactoring UI — loading/empty states
problem: The 7,144-paint catalog populates client-side from Dexie and takes ~2-3.5s before the swatch wall fills. During that window the SWATCHES panel can render empty with no skeleton/loading indicator. LIST and FILTER controls also depend on the same data. (Functionality is correct once populated — LIST view and FILTER slide-out are both implemented.)
fix: Add a loading skeleton / 'Loading 7,144 paints...' indicator to the SWATCHES/PAINTS panel until Dexie reports ready (>1s waits need progress). Optionally disable GRID/LIST/FILTER toggles until data is present.

principle: Figma paint-info.png vs live; NN/g #4 consistency
problem: Minor Figma-vs-live deltas in the paint-info slide-out: (a) Figma button reads 'MARK AS WANTED' (green-bordered), live reads '☆ Wishlist' (yellow — yellow is the agreed wishlist colour, but the label differs from Figma); (b) the live panel adds a 'MATCH — closest across brands' section not in the Figma ref (an enhancement); (c) HARMONIES scheme uses a native <select> (covered by UX-007). Overall the panel is a strong match.
fix: Confirm with Ross that the 'MATCH' section and the 'Wishlist' label (vs Figma 'MARK AS WANTED') are intended. No code change unless Figma-exact wording is wanted.

principle: Refactoring UI — fewer borders / spacing communicates grouping (polish, not a defect)
location: project tables and panels (cyan/20 hairline borders + corner ticks)
problem: The app leans on 1px cyan hairline borders + corner ticks for nearly every panel. On-brand for the CRT aesthetic and reads well, but in the densest tables (dashboard projects, collection) the uniform border weight slightly flattens hierarchy between row groups. Not a defect — a polish opportunity.
fix: Optional: in the densest tables, use background-tint banding or extra row spacing to separate row groups (Refactoring UI 'fewer borders') while keeping the terminal frame. Low priority / taste call.
